article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Sativa-leaning hybrid
Genetics: MK-Ultra × Creamsicle × Lemon Fizz F2
Breeder: Calyx Bros Seed Co.
THC Content: 20-24%
CBD Content: Typically below 1%
Terpene Profile: limonene , pinene , caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Lemon, mandarin orange, lime, sour citrus
Flowering Time (Indoor): Approximately 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: early to mid-October
Indoor Yield: Large
Outdoor Yield: High
Grow Difficulty: Intermediate

Yuzu belongs to the small group of cannabis strains whose name accurately prepares you for what happens when the jar opens. Instead of using “citrus” as a vague background descriptor, this cultivar can deliver an almost concentrated blast of lemon peel, mandarin, lime, tart orange, and sweet tropical fruit. Calyx Bros. Seed Co. bred the plant specifically around that aromatic intensity, comparing its scent to every citrus fruit compressed into one exceptionally powerful bouquet. The result is weed with a bright, penetrating nose that can feel closer to freshly grated citrus rind than the generalized lemon character found in many marijuana hybrids.

The genetics underneath that brightness are surprisingly heavy. MK-Ultra introduces G13 and OG Kush influence, while the Creamsicle parent adds sweeter fruit and creamy depth. Lemon Fizz contributes Super Lemon Haze together with Kakalak Kush, a Calyx Bros line containing Abusive Kush, Sour Diesel, Chem D, and additional Sour Diesel ancestry. Calyx Bros therefore created Yuzu from a mixture of haze, OG, Chem, Sour, and sweeter fruit genetics rather than simply crossing two lemon strains. That layered pedigree helps explain why stronger expressions can move from sharp citrus into herbs, Kush, fuel, and earth as the flowers are broken apart.
Genetics and Lineage

The maternal side begins with a Twisty Treat Seeds cross between MK-Ultra and Creamsicle. Calyx Bros selected what it called the “Orange Wine” phenotype from that population, suggesting a specific emphasis on fruit intensity rather than using an arbitrary female. MK-Ultra itself is associated with G13 and OG Kush genetics, bringing substantial potency, earth, pine, and Kush-like depth. Creamsicle pulls the profile in the opposite direction with sweeter, softer fruit characteristics. That parent gives Yuzu some of the orange, cream, and ripe-fruit qualities that appear behind its more aggressive lemon notes.

Lemon Fizz F2 provides the male side and is essential to understanding the cultivar. Calyx Bros created Lemon Fizz from Super Lemon Haze × Kakalak Kush. The breeder describes its selected Lemon Fizz plants as extraordinarily aromatic, with lemon-drop candy intensity, large colas, strong trichome production, and a relatively low leaf-to-calyx ratio. Kakalak Kush adds Abusive Kush, Sour Diesel , Chem D , while Super Lemon Haze contributes the sharper haze-driven citrus and energetic character.

Crossing that Lemon Fizz F2 male back into the Orange Wine selection gave Yuzu several distinct aromatic routes to follow. Some plants can emphasize lemon and lime, others push toward mandarin or sweet orange, and still others reveal more Kush, spice, herbs, or tropical fruit beneath the citrus. The breeder described the variety as medium-tall with large yield potential and an eight-to-nine-week flowering period, indicating that the cross retained enough vigor and sativa influence to stretch without requiring an unusually long finish.
Effects and Experience

The early experience generally matches the brightness of the aroma. Moderate amounts can produce a noticeable cerebral lift, more active thought patterns, and a stronger interest in conversation, music, visual media, or creative work. Rather than pushing immediately toward physical heaviness, the first stage tends to feel alert and outward-facing. Mood may brighten rapidly, and familiar activities can feel more engaging without the abrupt mental pressure associated with some extremely racy sativas.

As the session develops, the Kush and heavier hybrid ancestry becomes easier to recognize. The initial stimulation usually settles into a more comfortable rhythm while the body begins to loosen. Physical relaxation is present without necessarily overwhelming the mental clarity, particularly at moderate doses. This progression gives the weed useful flexibility: smaller amounts may suit daytime or afternoon use, whereas larger quantities can turn the same cultivar into a considerably slower experience.

Potency should not be underestimated simply because the flavor feels light and refreshing. Contemporary Yuzu products have appeared around 22% THC, while secondary cultivar records commonly place stronger flower in roughly the low-to-mid 20% range. Because Calyx Bros did not establish a universal laboratory THC specification, the actual package certificate is more reliable than any fixed strain-wide percentage. Dry mouth, dry eyes, temporary memory impairment, dizziness, or anxiety remain possible when THC intake exceeds an individual’s tolerance.
Medical Benefits

Yuzu itself has not been evaluated in controlled clinical trials, meaning there is no scientific basis for claiming that this specific marijuana cultivar treats a particular disease. Its effects may nevertheless appeal to medical cannabis consumers who prefer an uplifting THC-dominant strain rather than an immediately sedating one. The combination of brighter mood, increased engagement, and later physical relaxation may fit patients looking for temporary help with appetite, stress, mild discomfort, or low daytime motivation.

The dose makes a major difference. A small or moderate amount may preserve alertness while changing mood and easing physical tension, whereas heavier consumption can undermine concentration or produce uncomfortable stimulation in THC-sensitive patients. Anyone prone to cannabis-related anxiety should be particularly conservative with stronger batches, since uplifting strains can become mentally intense when consumed rapidly.

Its striking aroma should also be separated from unsupported medical claims about terpenes. Citrus-heavy cannabis is often presumed to be dominated by limonene, but aroma alone cannot establish a reliable terpene percentage, and different Yuzu phenotypes may express different chemical profiles. Medical consumers should therefore use laboratory results from their particular harvest rather than assuming every sample has the same cannabinoids or terpenes.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Few cultivars make citrus the center of the experience as completely as Yuzu. Fresh flowers can smell like lemon zest, mandarin peel, lime juice, tart orange candy, and sweet tropical fruit all at once. Crushing the bud generally intensifies the acidic side of the profile, releasing a sharp aroma reminiscent of citrus oils from freshly peeled fruit. Calyx Bros specifically described the strain as combining the impression of many citrus fruits into one concentrated aroma.

Behind that initial explosion is a deeper layer inherited from the Kush, Chem, Sour, and MK-Ultra ancestry. Herbal spice, earth, mild fuel, and pine can become more noticeable after the brighter volatile compounds disperse. Some expressions also carry creamier orange notes from the Creamsicle side, producing a combination closer to orange sherbet or a citrus dessert than straight lemon.

Flavor follows a similar pattern. The inhale can be sour, tangy, and almost mouthwatering, with lemon and lime arriving before sweeter mandarin and tropical notes. Kush and herbal spice tend to show themselves more clearly on the exhale. A careful dry and cure is particularly important with this cannabis strain because excessive heat can strip away precisely the volatile citrus compounds that make the cultivar distinctive.
Growing Information

Calyx Bros breeder material describes Yuzu as a medium-to-tall plant with large yield potential and an indoor flowering period of roughly eight to nine weeks. That combination makes it relatively fast for a cultivar carrying considerable Super Lemon Haze influence. Growers should still expect noticeable vertical growth once flowering begins, especially from phenotypes that lean strongly toward the Lemon Fizz side.

Early topping, branch spreading, or other canopy management can help make better use of indoor lighting while preventing the tallest shoots from dominating the garden. The medium-tall architecture also makes spacing worthwhile; plants allowed to crowd each other can shade lower flowering sites and restrict airflow. As buds begin adding weight, branch support may become useful because the Lemon Fizz parent was selected in part for substantial flower production.

Phenotype selection may be particularly rewarding. The original seed population was created from a specifically selected Orange Wine female and Lemon Fizz F2 male rather than stabilized as an extremely uniform commercial clone. Growers hunting seed may therefore find meaningful differences in citrus character, plant height, flower shape, and finishing time. For a keeper, intense citrus aroma, resin production, structural strength, and a manageable flowering period may be more valuable criteria than yield alone.
FAQ
What are the genetics of the Yuzu strain?

The original Calyx Bros. Seed Co. Yuzu is (MK-Ultra × Creamsicle) × Lemon Fizz F2. The breeder used Twisty Treat Seeds’ MK-Ultra × Creamsicle Orange Wine phenotype and crossed it with its own Lemon Fizz F2 male.
Who bred Yuzu?

Yuzu was bred by Calyx Bros. Seed Co. The name has since been used for other unrelated marijuana cultivars, so lineage should be checked before assuming every product labeled Yuzu represents the Calyx Bros genetics.
Is Yuzu indica or sativa?

The Calyx Bros version is best described as a sativa-leaning hybrid. Its early effects tend to feel cerebral, uplifting, and active, while OG, G13, Kush, and Chem-related ancestry adds a progressively relaxing physical component.
What does Yuzu weed taste like?

Citrus dominates the profile, particularly lemon, lime, mandarin orange, and tart citrus peel. Sweeter tropical fruit, cream, herbs, earth, Kush, and occasional fuel-like notes can appear underneath depending on phenotype and cultivation.
How long does Yuzu take to flower?

The breeder lists approximately eight to nine weeks of indoor flowering. Plants are described as medium-tall with large yield potential, although exact finishing time can vary between phenotypes and growing environments.
Final Thoughts on Yuzu

Yuzu stands apart because its citrus identity comes from deliberate breeding rather than a convenient marketing name. Calyx Bros selected an Orange Wine phenotype from MK-Ultra × Creamsicle and paired it with a Lemon Fizz F2 male already chosen for extraordinary lemon intensity. Underneath that flavor-focused pairing sits a complex foundation involving Super Lemon Haze, OG Kush, G13, Chem D, Sour Diesel, Abusive Kush, and additional sweet fruit genetics.

The result is a cultivar capable of balancing exceptionally bright aroma with considerably darker genetic depth. Lemon, lime, mandarin, and sweet orange dominate the surface, while Kush, herbs, earth, and occasional fuel make the flavor increasingly complex as the flower is consumed. The experience follows a similar path, moving from energetic cerebral engagement toward smoother body relaxation rather than staying narrowly stimulating.

Its reputation has also continued to grow well beyond the original seed release. A Yuzu entry cultivated by Ball Family Farms placed third for Best Terps/Smell at the 2025 California Zalympix, demonstrating how competitive the cultivar’s aromatic potential can be when the right selection is grown well. For citrus-focused cannabis enthusiasts, Yuzu remains a particularly compelling example of flavor-driven breeding backed by enough Kush, Chem, haze, and Sour ancestry to give the weed substance beyond its unmistakable fruit character.
